name: End-to-end capstone
description: Compose the validated primitives into read-only and write-capable orchestration capstones without introducing a new primitive.

variants.description: Run a visible multi-agent research factory that plans, fans out, verifies a local browser fixture, synthesizes, notifies, and tears down without writes.
setup: Create a secret-free disposable repository and local browser fixture, choose a small read-only research request, and capture the baseline Cmux tree.
Create one run-owned group, start event listeners, record provider roles, and define structured plan, shard, verification, synthesis, and teardown artifacts.
exercise: Have the root orchestrator produce a plan, fan independent read-only shards to agents, update status from correlated events, and collect every artifact.
Run deterministic tests and local browser checks, synthesize evidence, emit one non-sensitive completion notification, and tear down the fleet.

assertions.expectation: The plan defines independent roles, ownership, verifier commands, deadlines, and artifact paths before dispatch.
Every planned shard has exactly one terminal artifact or explicit failure record in the final synthesis.
Local tests and browser checks produce machine-readable evidence and no console errors.
The disposable repository remains unchanged despite multi-agent execution.
One notification and result report remain while all agents, listeners, surfaces, workspaces, and groups are reclaimed.

cleanup: Stop providers and listeners, close resources in dependency order using the ownership ledger, and clear run-owned notifications if requested.
Delete fixtures after retaining a redacted evidence summary and prove the unrelated baseline is unchanged.

variants.description: Implement one bounded fixture feature through isolated writer worktrees, integrate explicitly, verify, collect a diff, notify, and tear down.
setup: Create a disposable parent repository with a small seeded feature request, tests, local browser fixture, and no remotes or secrets.
Create one worktree per writer, define non-overlapping ownership, choose an explicit integrator, start listeners, and record the full ownership ledger.
exercise: Plan the change, fan out only independent owned files, require per-writer tests and diffs, and stop or reassign workers only under the cancellation policy.
Have the integrator apply reviewed diffs to an integration worktree, run the complete test and browser suite, collect one final patch, notify, and tear down.

assertions.expectation: Every writer modifies only its owned worktree and declared files; no two writers edit the same path concurrently.
The integration record names every accepted or rejected writer diff and the reason for its disposition.
The integration worktree passes the full test suite, expected UI behavior, and clean console/error checks.
One reviewable final patch contains only the requested fixture feature and no generated secrets or unrelated changes.
All worktrees, agents, listeners, browser/server processes, surfaces, workspaces, and groups are removed without touching unrelated resources.

cleanup: Stop all agents and local servers, close owned Cmux resources, and remove writer worktrees only after final evidence is collected.
Delete the disposable parent repository, clear run-owned notifications if requested, and compare the full post-run tree with the baseline.
